headline: High: shared filesystem/git and overlapping write/network capabilities make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads repo files and user-provided directories, and dbt-core consumes warehouse-facing inputs; if Claude Code writes instructions into shared files, dbt-core can ingest them as trusted content. The pair shares state via filesystem/git only, so the interaction is plausible without extra tooling, though not directly documented for dbt-core.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or git branch
IF dbt-core parses files produced by Claude Code as authoritative inputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit provenance markers on files before dbt-core reads them
Disable automatic ingestion of Claude Code-generated artifacts
Review shared files before dbt-core execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data. Because Claude Code has broad network egress and both agents can share files via filesystem/git, sensitive code or warehouse-derived data can cross boundaries in default workflows, even though dbt-core’s outbound behavior is only partially documented.
conditions: IF the same repository or working directory contains secrets or warehouse extracts
IF Claude Code or dbt-core is pointed at files containing sensitive data
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared repos
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict Claude Code network access during sensitive work
Run dbt-core only on sanitized datasets
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the pair shares state via filesystem and git only. dbt-core is not shown to lock shared mutable resources, so concurrent edits can clobber files or git history in default multi-instance use. Uncertainty about dbt-core locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same git checkout
IF either agent writes generated artifacts into the shared workspace
mitigations: Serialize writes to the repo
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Add file locks around generated artifacts
Run one agent in a separate clone
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code and file edits that dbt-core may consume as inputs, and dbt-core can then act on those artifacts in warehouse workflows. There is no documented verification step between them, so mistakes or hallucinated transformations can propagate across multiple work products, though direct action-taking authority is limited.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes SQL/models generated by Claude Code without review
IF generated artifacts are deployed to analytics workflows
mitigations: Add human review before dbt runs
Compare generated diffs against expected patterns
Pin dbt execution to reviewed branches
Require tests before deployment
Document a verification checklist

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and broad local files, while dbt-core touches warehouse data. If warehouse data includes regulated or residency-bound records, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches because Claude Code runs locally on the host and dbt-core’s warehouse handling is not shown to enforce the same controls. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the shared workspace or warehouse
IF the warehouse contains data subject to residency or retention constraints
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared files
Confirm retention settings in the warehouse
Use a DPA-approved deployment path
Limit Claude Code access to non-regulated repos
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
